- When sentiment is consistently negative or near-zero over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply a 3–5% downward adjustment to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ days), model frequently overestimates upward trend; cap forecast growth at 2–3% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add a 1–2% downward bias to forecast if sentiment drops below 0.20.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate downward moves in low-sentiment periods; increase forecast by 2–4% if sentiment remains flat or negative for 5+ days.
- If sentiment is volatile or erratic, model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying sentiment-adjusted correction.
